testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How should you test a parking brake?

options.text: The engine should not be running.
Put the vehicle in low gear and try to pull forward.
Have a professional mechanic inspect it.
Drive the vehicle with the parking brake on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and try to pull forward.
questions.explanation: To test a parking brake, fasten your seat belt, set the parking brake, release the trailer parking brake if needed, put the vehicle in low gear, and try to pull forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it needs repair.

questions.question: What is true about dual tires?

options.text: They do not both need to touch the road.
They should not touch each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not touch each other.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, check that dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.correctAnswerText: It varies by vehicle
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their brake systems.

questions.question: In bad weather, what do many drivers do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow closely behind trucks
questions.explanation: In bad weather with poor visibility, many drivers follow trucks closely. Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead if you are being followed too closely.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It cannot work with air brakes
It should only be used on dry roads
It helps you keep control when braking
It only works if all axles have ABS

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you keep control when braking
questions.explanation: ABS works with air brake systems. It helps keep your vehicle under control and prevents wheels from locking up during hard braking on slippery surfaces. ABS works even if only one axle has it.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes too much
questions.explanation: When brakes are overused, they get too hot. This heat causes them to fade and work less effectively.

questions.question: What should you do when visibility is poor at dawn or dusk?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights on
questions.explanation: When driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to help others see you.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when you accelerate on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: What mirrors should a registered vehicle have?

options.text: A mirror on the left side only
Mirrors on both the left and right sides
A mirror on the right side only

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors on both the left and right sides
questions.explanation: For safe driving, you need to see all sides of your vehicle. A vehicle must have mirrors on both sides and they should be checked regularly.

questions.question: What is true about a dual air brake system?

options.text: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines
The systems share air tanks but have separate hoses and lines
Each system uses the same lines and hoses
One system is primary and the other is a backup

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share one brake control, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Take a pill to stay awake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get some sleep.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and get sleep. This is the only safe action. Driving while tired is dangerous and can cause serious crashes. Pills may keep you awake for a short time, but they will not make you more alert.

questions.question: Which of these is acceptable to find during a pre-trip tire inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different companies
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every trip. Tire sizes must match. Tires must not have cuts, cracks, or other damage.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, what should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your four-way flashers
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you park on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate must not be higher than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brakes squeak, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then press it firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake problem.

questions.question: If a vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, the driver should:

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it
Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks
Try to flag down another vehicle for a push
Wait in the vehicle for a police officer

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is stuck on railroad tracks, get out immediately and walk away. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call that number or call 911.

questions.question: A skid caused by acceleration can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Removing your foot from the accelerator

questions.correctAnswerText: Removing your foot from the accelerator
questions.explanation: Skids from acceleration often happen on slippery roads. You can usually fix these skids by releasing the accelerator.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away, so mechanical force is needed to hold the brakes on.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Leave the keys in the ignition

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil and grease.
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, check for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make items stand taller in a trailer.
Prevent items from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload items from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo. Bracing connects from the top of cargo to the floor and sides of the trailer.

questions.question: When spring brakes are activated in an air brake vehicle, never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: Do not push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Combining spring brake force with air brake pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can allow poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can allow poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, check for all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers.
questions.explanation: Check that tires have at least 4/32 inch tread depth in front tires and 2/32 inch in other tires. Make sure tires are not worn, cracked, or low on air, and are all the same size.

questions.question: Hanging meat cargo is usually:

options.text: Dangerous, due to the possible scent.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unstable.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat cargo is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the swinging motion affects how the driver can control the vehicle.

questions.question: Blocking cargo:

options.text: Should be done to prevent cargo from shifting.
Can only be done with metal pieces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done to prevent cargo from shifting.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing keep cargo from shifting during transport. Block cargo on the front, back, and sides to prevent movement.

questions.question: Passive railroad crossings:

options.text: Are not controlled by any traffic control device.
Have gates that lower when trains are approaching.
Should never be crossed by a CMV.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not controlled by any traffic control device.
questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: You must place emergency warning devices within ____ of stopping on the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 minutes
questions.explanation: Place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the road. Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when pulling off the road.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you when you need to brake?

options.text: Tap your brakes lightly a few times.
Stick your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes lightly a few times.
questions.explanation: Light taps on the brake pedal make your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because it is harder to see hazards in the dark.

questions.question: When approaching a bridge or overpass, you should:

options.text: Trust that the posted clearance height is correct.
Not assume the posted clearance height is accurate.
Measure the height of the opening before going under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the posted clearance height is accurate.
questions.explanation: Do not trust posted height signs. The road may have been repaved or snow may be on the ground, changing the actual clearance. If you are unsure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, you can help by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your lights on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights when visibility is low. If you cannot see others, they cannot see you.

questions.question: On a wet road, reduce your speed by:
questions.correctAnswerText: About one-third.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads. Slippery surfaces make it harder to stop and turn, so slower speeds are necessary.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Keep your vehicle in a straight line while stopping.
Expect your vehicle to slow down faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle in a straight line while stopping.
questions.explanation: Use controlled or stab braking to stop in a straight line. This keeps your vehicle stable and lets you turn if needed.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times can:

options.text: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the brake system.
Make the brake pedal harder to press.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: On vehicles with air brakes, unnecessary brake pedal use releases air faster than the compressor can replace it. This can lower air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: Once stopped during the stop/start test, you should:

options.text: Not use four-way flashers because it is only a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes
questions.explanation: Light brake taps make your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: After starting a trip with cargo, you should:

options.text: Only inspect the cargo if someone tells you there is a problem.
Inspect the cargo within the first 50 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the cargo within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every 3 hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of a vehicle fire?
questions.correctAnswerText: Rolling down the window
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can be caused by: spilled fuel or improper use of flares after a crash; under-inflated tires or dual tires touching; electrical system short circuits; smoking near fuel; improper fueling or loose fuel connections; and flammable cargo that is improperly sealed, loaded, or ventilated.

questions.question: How do states verify that a CDL or CLP driver has only one license?

options.text: By making phone calls to surrounding states.
By using a computerized system that connects all states.
By looking through the driver's wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a computerized system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP license information in a computerized database. When you apply for a license in one state, that state checks this database to make sure you do not already have a license in another state.

questions.question: What is the correct stab braking method for an emergency stop?

options.text: Push the brakes all the way until the wheels lock, release the brakes until the wheels roll again, then repeat.
Push the brakes about halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Push the brakes all the way and hold them down while the wheels stay locked until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes all the way until the wheels lock, release the brakes until the wheels roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking for emergency stops means: push the brakes all the way until they lock, release the brakes until the wheels start rolling, then repeat this process.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones. Always slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Stay as far away from the flames as possible.
Use any extinguisher on every type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the flames as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay as far away from a fire as possible. Aim the extinguisher at the source or base of the fire, not at the flames. Some fires may be treated with water. If you are unsure how to treat a fire, wait for trained firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: Who is responsible for checking a vehicle's cargo?

options.text: The owner of the trucking company

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for inspecting their cargo. Drivers must check that cargo is not overloaded or poorly balanced, is properly secured, does not block their view, and does not restrict access to emergency equipment. The driver is always responsible, even if someone else loaded and secured the cargo.

questions.question: How does friction work in an S-cam brake?

options.text: The brake shoes and linings push against the outside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes and linings push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: In an S-cam brake, friction is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What condition may be needed to check automatic transmission fluid?

options.text: The vehicle should be on an incline.
The vehicle should be on a decline.
The engine may need to be running.
The vehicle should be lifted with a jack.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine may need to be running.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When will an applicant be denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: If they are a U.S. citizen.
If they are wanted for a misdemeanor.
If they are wanted for certain felonies.
If they already have a driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: If they are wanted for certain felonies.
questions.explanation: A hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you: do not have legal permanent status in the U.S.; renounce U.S. citizenship; are wanted for, under indictment for, or convicted of certain felonies; are judged mentally incompetent or involuntarily committed to a mental institution; or are considered a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only when it is wet outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: To drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from air brake system tanks. When you use a drain, make sure to drain the tank completely.
